spec_disagreements: Base commit. The spec body and your brief both say the base is b63a8368. The worktree HEAD is 6ab9d7ea, with W4-1 merged as PR #173, which is what the rulings require. Every body anchor after W4-1's insertion has moved: url stamp price_service :9845 → :10203; extract_price_from_shopping :9681 → :9997; stash stamp scs :8276 → :8319; park :6652 → :6657; backfill :7661-7663 → :7666-7667; extract_price_from_html :13166 → :13522. The spec's §5 byte-identity step says to re-run the base from a detached checkout of b63a8368; per the rulings it must be 6ab9d7ea, or byte-identity would be measured across W4-1.

Gate 1's expected colouring is wrong. It expects '2/4/5/6/10/11/12 green before any edit'. Test 10, the flag reader, cannot be green before the reader exists. It is red at HEAD, and reddens on an assertion under a stub. Test 6's live half is red at HEAD under R7, because the url is still there.

Gate 2 says to deselect every id in tests/.pre_impl_failures.txt '(89 lines)'. The file does have 89 lines, but 78 are comments and only 11 are node ids. I ran without `--deselect`, matching your standing shape, so the baseline failures show up and can be checked against the file.
Gate 2's grep count '= 288 files' is stale. At 6ab9d7ea the spec's own pattern matches 290 files and your pattern matches 307. I ran the 309-file union.

The comm shape as written cannot finish on this Windows box without additions. Both unguarded halves were killed by pytest-timeout's thread method, which exits the whole process. The unguarded run also reached real network endpoints: api.openai.com with the dummy key (no credentials, since there is no .env and conftest strips them) and the neutralized supabase sentinel. That is a network touch you told me to avoid, and I am reporting it. The recorded base adds a loopback-only socket and DNS guard plus an openai/platform import warm-up. The head run must use the same tools, saved in .qa-w4/comm_tools/.

The claim that the base fails only on baseline ids does not hold. The comm base has one failure missing from tests/.pre_impl_failures.txt: tests/test_shopify_discovery_l13.py::TestFetchShopifyPrice::test_fetch_uses_catalog_and_matches. The code it runs does a real curl_cffi catalog fetch despite the test's patched `_fetch_shopify_catalog`. libcurl DNS times out after 17.5 s and bypasses any Python socket guard. It is a network-dependent test that existed before this unit.

§3 Preserve and §7 limit 1 say 'this unit cannot cache anything new' and 'select_best(require_url=True) drops a discovery-only row'. That holds only with ENABLE_EXACT_PRICE_GATE ON. Measured with the gate false: should_cache_price is True and select_best returns the url-less row. This is consistent with R7's gate-off note, but the body's general wording is wrong for the rollback state.
